title: releasecut.bats's 0335 arm names its own gate cache bound, so its keep rests on no runner's free disk
objective: releasecut.bats's 0335 arm ("release gates hands its gates DEVBIN_GATE_CACHE, .gate-cache in the project's directory under the cache root, made when missing and kept from run to run, and the one the environment names instead") names its own gate cache bound, so that its "kept from run to run" does not rest on the runner's free disk. The arm sets no `release.gate_cache.max`, so the 12G default applies. Since I14a851d, `gate_cache_bound` (lib/release.legs) keeps a cache within its bound only while its disk has the bound free. On a disk with less than 12G free, the arm's second run empties the cache, and the arm reads one line where it wants two. The fix gives the arm's fixture a small bound, eg `gate_cache: max: 1M`, as the 0361 arm beside it does, or a df stand-in. Size XS.
body:
The red. On devbin 0.1.35's candidate run 45956129632, at the release commit f257282e, the WSL job (Ubuntu 26.04 in WSL 2) failed one arm of 3290, this one, test 2353, at line 4698: "the directory did not keep the first run's line for the second: run". Every other job was green, and the WSL job blocks nothing, so the release stands. The job's log names no free size.

The trace (dc's close-out run co1127, 2026-11-27 09:16Z by date -u, on a Desk grant). The arm ran unchanged at a tip whose lib/ and tests/ are f257282e's, with a df stand-in first on PATH. With the disk reading 4194304 KiB free, a third of the 12582912 KiB default, the arm went red at line 4698 with the WSL job's words. The output of its second run read: "release: gates: <cache>/demo/.gate-cache held 4 KiB, within its bound of 12582912 KiB, with 4194304 KiB free on its disk, under the bound, so it is emptied and this run builds cold". With the disk reading 16777216 KiB free, the arm went green. By the code, the free-space rule is the one path that empties the cache between the arm's two runs. So the WSL runner's disk under TMPDIR had less than 12G free. That is inferred from the trace and the code, not read on the runner.

Reach. This is the one arm that expects this machine's cache kept under the default bound. The 0361 arm beside it names `max: 1M`. A remote leg's start holds its cache only when it is handed a bound, and releaselegs.bats's 0335 arm hands none. An Ubuntu or macOS runner with less than 12G free under TMPDIR turns this arm red there too. Test Summary waits for those jobs, so a cut would stop.

Proof for the fix. The arm red at its base under the df stand-in reading a third of the bound free, and green at the tip under the same stand-in. Green under the system's df. Then the next candidate's WSL job green.
